findings.desc: CONTRADICTING: In a solid-phase interaction assay, ApoE3 and ApoE4 bound the recycling receptor Apoer2 with similar affinity (only ApoE2 bound poorly), so at the level of initial receptor binding ApoE4 does not adhere more tightly than ApoE3; the isoform difference in this paper arises after endocytosis, in endosomes. This paper reports no endosomal dissociation/binding-affinity assay of its own.
findings.exp_system: Cell-derived naturally secreted ApoE isoform particles incubated with Apoer2-Fc (secreted Apoer2 ectodomain) on protein-G beads; co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot
findings.quote: ApoE3 and ApoE4 bind Apoer2 with similar affinity, whereas ApoE2 binding to Apoer2 is poor.
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no increase in binding affinity for Apoer2 in a solid-phase assay) [CONTRADICTS]

findings.desc: In primary neurons, Apoer2 recycled back to the cell surface quickly in the presence of ApoE3 but its reappearance was greatly delayed with ApoE4, and co-immunoprecipitation showed prolonged retention of ApoE4 compared with ApoE3 in Apoer2-containing intracellular compartments, i.e. ApoE4 impedes Apoer2 recycling.
findings.exp_system: Primary rat cortical neurons treated with cell-derived ApoE3- or ApoE4-conditioned media plus Reelin; cell-surface biotinylation recycling assay and Apoer2 co-immunoprecipitation
findings.quote: While Apoer2 quickly recycled in the presence of ApoE3, its reappearance on the cell surface was greatly delayed in the presence of ApoE4 (Figure 2B,C).
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (delayed Apoer2 recycling and prolonged ApoE retention in Apoer2-containing endosomes)

findings.desc: Pharmacological and genetic inhibition of the early-endosomal proton leak channel NHE6 completely reversed the ApoE4-induced recycling block of Apoer2/Lrp8 and of the co-endocytosed AMPA- and NMDA-type glutamate receptors, showing the ApoE4 recycling block is reversible by lowering endosomal pH away from ApoE4's isoelectric point.
findings.exp_system: Primary neurons treated with ApoE4-conditioned media and Reelin, with the NHE inhibitor EMD87580 or NHE6-specific shRNAs; surface and total Apoer2 immunoblot
findings.quote: We found that pharmacological and genetic inhibition of NHE6, the primary proton leak channel in the early endosome, in rodents completely reverses the ApoE4-induced recycling block of the ApoE receptor Apoer2/Lrp8 and the AMPA- and NMDA-type glutamate receptors that are regulated by, and co-endocytosed in a complex with, Apoer2.
findings.summary: (NHE6 inhibition) -> (complete reversal of the ApoE4-induced Apoer2 recycling block)

findings.desc: Class 5 (other): this paper states the H4 adhesion mechanism as its framing premise, summarising prior work rather than measuring dissociation itself in a new assay here: because ApoE4's isoelectric point matches early-endosomal pH, ApoE4 dissociates late from ApoE receptors, impairing endolysosomal trafficking.
findings.exp_system: Mechanism statement in the abstract of a mouse NHE6 (Slc9a6) depletion study, summarising the ApoE4 delayed-dissociation model from the same research programme
findings.quote: The isoelectric point of ApoE4 matches the pH of the early endosome (EE), causing its delayed dissociation from ApoE receptors and hence impaired endolysosomal trafficking, disruption of synaptic homeostasis, and reduced amyloid clearance.
findings.summary: (APOE4 at early-endosomal pH) -> (delayed dissociation from ApoE receptors and impaired endolysosomal trafficking)

findings.desc: In primary neurons, ApoE-conditioned media reduced surface expression of Apoer2 and glutamate receptors in the presence of Reelin, with a stronger reduction by ApoE4 than ApoE3, and genetic NHE6 depletion counteracted the ApoE4-induced reduction, experimentally reproducing the ApoE4 recycling impairment and its rescue.
findings.exp_system: Primary neurons from wild-type and Slc9a6-knockout (NHE6-deficient) littermate mice treated with naturally secreted ApoE3 or ApoE4 and/or Reelin; cell-surface biotinylation assay for Apoer2, GluN2B, GluA1 and GluA2/3
findings.quote: Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3. NHE6 depletion counteracts the ApoE4-induced reduction of receptor surface expression.
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (stronger loss of surface Apoer2/glutamate receptors; reversed by NHE6 depletion)

findings.desc: Direct quantitative binding assays (HTRF and surface plasmon resonance) showed lipidated ApoE4 and ApoE3 both bind the LDL receptor with high, comparable affinity (SPR KD 9 nM for ApoE4 vs 16 nM for ApoE3), while lipidated ApoE2 bound ~50-fold more weakly (KD 800 nM); ApoE4 is therefore at most marginally tighter-binding than ApoE3, and the study's main binding contrast is ApoE3/E4 versus ApoE2.
findings.exp_system: POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms binding to LDLR extracellular domain; HTRF and surface plasmon resonance (Biacore) binding assays
findings.quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D).
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (comparable high-affinity LDLR binding, KD 16 nM -> 9 nM; both far tighter than APOE2)

findings.desc: Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, but not ApoE2, reduced cell-surface LDLR and trapped LDLR in endolysosomal compartments, i.e. stronger-binding isoforms impair LDLR recycling; the study groups ApoE3 with ApoE4 and does NOT separate ApoE4 from ApoE3 on the recycling defect, so it supports a binding-strength-to-recycling coupling without an ApoE4-over-ApoE3 gradient.
findings.exp_system: H4 neuroglioma cells, WT HAP1 cells and human APOE-KO iPSC-derived astrocytes treated 1 day with lipidated ApoE isoforms; immunostaining of cell-surface and total LDLR
findings.quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake (Figure 2A–D, Figure S2A–B).
findings.summary: (APOE2 -> APOE3/APOE4) -> (reduced surface LDLR and impaired LDLR recycling, with no APOE4-vs-APOE3 separation)

findings.desc: ApoE binds the insulin receptor (a recycling receptor, though not a canonical ApoE receptor) in an isoform-dependent manner, with ApoE4 showing higher binding affinity than ApoE3 in solid-phase binding assays, confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation of more insulin receptor with ApoE4 than ApoE3.
findings.exp_system: Recombinant apoE and astrocyte-secreted lipidated apoE particles binding to insulin receptor; solid-phase binding assay and solution co-immunoprecipitation
findings.quote: Taken together, these data demonstrated that apoE binds to IR in an isoform-dependent manner with apoE4 showing higher binding affinity than apoE3.
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher binding affinity for the insulin receptor)

findings.desc: ApoE4 interfered with insulin binding to its receptor more than ApoE3: apoE4 reduced insulin-insulin receptor binding by nearly 50%, significantly more than the 25% reduction by apoE3, in a competitive solid-phase binding assay.
findings.exp_system: Competitive solid-phase binding assay of insulin (8 nM), insulin receptor (80 nM) and apoE3 or apoE4 (4-16 μg/ml)
findings.quote: When apoE was co-incubated with insulin and IR, we found that apoE4 (16 μg/ml) reduced insulin-IR binding by nearly 50%, which is significantly higher than apoE3 treatment (25%) (Figure 5F).

findings.desc: ApoE4 trapped the insulin receptor in endosomes and impaired its recycling: nearly 20% of IR-GFP co-localised with transferrin-positive endosomes in apoE4-treated neuronal cells versus less with apoE3, and biotinylation recycling assays showed significantly more intracellular insulin receptor retained at 30 and 60 min with apoE4.
findings.exp_system: SH-SY5Y neuronal cells expressing human IR-GFP and Apoe-knockout primary cortical neurons treated with recombinant apoE3 or apoE4; transferrin co-localisation imaging and cell-surface biotinylation recycling assay
findings.quote: In the absence of insulin, we found that nearly 20% of IR-GFP co-localized with transferrin in the endosomal compartment in apoE4-treated cells whereas less co-localization was observed in apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6A and 6D).
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (insulin receptor trapped in transferrin-positive endosomes and delayed receptor recycling)

findings.desc: In CHO cells co-expressing sortilin and its cargo FABP7, apoE4 lowered FABP7 levels compared with apoE3, i.e. apoE4 binding blocks sortilin-mediated sorting of its cargo; the measured readout is sorting/stability of the cargo FABP7, not sortilin's own surface recycling, making this the least direct test of the hypothesis among the five papers.
findings.exp_system: CHO cells stably co-expressing sortilin and FABP7 (CHO-S/F) treated 24 h with HEK293 conditioned medium containing 5 μg/ml apoE3 or apoE4; Western blot and densitometry
findings.quote: levels of FABP7 in CHO-S/F cells were significantly lowered by the addition of apoE4 as compared with apoE3 (Fig. 7A,B).
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower FABP7 levels via blocked sortilin-mediated cargo sorting)

findings.desc: Proximity ligation showed sortilin-FABP7 complexes redistribute from a dispersed vesicular pattern with apoE3 to a perinuclear pattern with apoE4, with altered co-localisation with Rab5 early endosomes and Rab11 recycling endosomes, indicating apoE4 misroutes sortilin complexes; again the readout is cargo-complex routing rather than sortilin recycling itself.
findings.exp_system: CHO-S/F cells treated with apoE3- or apoE4-conditioned medium; proximity ligation assay for sortilin-FABP7 complexes with Rab5/Rab11 co-localisation
findings.quote: PLA signals for sortilin–FABP7 complexes change from a dispersed vesicular pattern with apoE3 to a perinuclear pattern with apoE4 (arrowheads).
findings.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (sortilin-FABP7 complexes misrouted to a perinuclear pattern, away from normal endosomal sorting)
